stories.headline: Stick-carrying groups threaten Delhi Election Commission protestors after arrests
stories.title: Stick-carrying groups threaten Delhi Election Commission protestors after arrests
stories.summary: Stick-carrying groups threaten Delhi Election Commission protestors after arrests
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Stick-carrying men again confronted protesters in central Delhi after Saturday's assaults.
The incidents have intensified scrutiny of police response and Hindu Raksha Dal's role.

Men carrying sticks were seen moving around central Delhi on Sunday and threatening demonstrators a day after saffron-clad groups assaulted protesters demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.
Police said four men had been arrested in connection with one of Saturday's assaults.
Even after the arrests, groups of men continued to move through protest sites in Connaught Place and other parts of the city.

On Saturday, thousands of protesters were detained across the capital during demonstrations over alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls carried out by it.

On Saturday, groups of men wearing saffron scarves and raising religious slogans were seen moving around protest areas, threatening demonstrators and openly backing the use of violence against those protesting against the Election Commission.
On Sunday, several men carrying sticks were again seen in Connaught Place, where demonstrations were taking place, confronting protesters and issuing threats.
The groups were seen moving about despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita being in force.

While four men claiming to be members of the right-wing Hindu Raksha Dal have been arrested for allegedly assaulting students and manhandling women on DDU Marg, videos from Saturday showed larger groups moving around protest areas in full view of police personnel, openly expressing support for them and the administration and threatening demonstrators.
The men were heard saying they had come out in support of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and did not care if the police picked them up.
They also alleged that "anti-national and anti-Modi" slogans were being raised at the protests, while some described the demonstrators as "anti-national elements" who "deserved to be thrashed".

stories.headline: Mehbooba flags risks of high-rise construction
stories.title: Mehbooba flags risks of high-rise construction
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 11: Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti on Sunday raised concerns over the opening up of agricultural land and orchards in Jammu and Kashmir for commercial high-rise construction, warning that such development could threaten food security and expose people to serious seismic risks. In a post on X, the former chief minister questioned the government's development approach, alleging that agricultural and horticultural land was being made available for commercial construction despite warnings about earthquake-related hazards. “In the name of development, J&K’s orchards and agricultural land are being opened up for commercial high rises, even as experts warn of catastrophic seismic and liquefaction risks,” Mehbooba said. She described the alleged changes as a threat not only to the region's agricultural resources but also to the safety of people living in areas vulnerable to natural disasters. “This is not development. It is a dangerous betrayal of our land, our food security and our people’s lives,” she said. The PDP president also questioned accountability in the event of a disaster arising from construction in vulnerable areas. “Who will take responsibility when this reckless experiment turns into a disaster?” she asked. Her remarks come amid criticism of changes to building and land-use regulations in Jammu and Kashmir, with opposition leaders questioning their implications for urban planning, agricultural land protection and environmental safety. However, Mehbooba did not identify specific projects or provide details of the expert assessments referred to in her post. Her claims regarding the extent of land opened for commercial construction remain unverified.

opening: The Saudi civil aviation authority on Sunday announced an attack on Dammam airport in the kingdom's Eastern Province, in a statement released shortly after the Iran-aligned Houthis said they had targeted the airport.
The attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam occured soon after a projectile struck a passenger terminal at the international airport in Riyadh.
body: Also read: 1 Indian dead, 10 injured in Riyadh airport attack; Houthis claim responsibilityEarlier on Saturday, a missile had hit the same terminal, killing more than ten people and injuring at least 300 people at the site.
The Houthis claimed responsibility for the attacks at Riyadh Airport and others.
Saudi authorities said there were injuries in the latest attack on the King Khalid International Airport complex for terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights, AP reported.
The missile attack on Saturday was the deadliest in a Gulf Arab nation since the Iran war began, with around 300 people wounded, some critically.
The authorities announced closure of the airport, which remained closed on Sunday.

The Houthis claimed responsibility for the attacks at Riyadh Airport and others.

stories.title: Delhi Metro shuts 6 stations amid Opposition's march to Supreme Court today

article_sentences: Delhi Metro has shut entry and exit at six stations, including Rajiv Chowk and Central Secretariat, from 6 am to 4 pm on October 12 over security concerns.
The restrictions come as Opposition parties plan a march to the Supreme Court against alleged "vote chori".
Interchange facilities will remain available.

The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has announced the closure of entry and exit gates at six metro stations from 6 am to 4 pm on Monday, October 12, citing security reasons, as Opposition parties prepare to march to the Supreme Court against alleged “vote chori”.
In a late-night post on X, the DMRC said entry and exit would remain closed at Patel Chowk, Janpath, Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, Central Secretariat and Barakhamba Road.
Interchange facilities will remain available at all six stations.
The DMRC said the situation would be reviewed by security agencies and further updates would be issued accordingly.

The restrictions come as Opposition parties under the INDIA bloc prepare to hold a protest march to the Supreme Court, demanding action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of electoral malpractice.

The protest, titled “Chalo Delhi – March for Democracy”, is expected to press for Kumar's resignation, a halt to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and a return to the paper ballot system.

Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, the Leaders of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha respectively, had sought an appointment with Chief Justice of India Surya Kant between 4 pm and 5 pm on Monday to submit a memorandum outlining their concerns.
However, sources told India Today that the CJI declined the request, citing the fact that similar matters were already pending before the Supreme Court.
His response was emailed to both leaders, the sources said.

article_sentences: A drone attack struck tanker Mt Petro Dolphin at Sohar Anchorage in Oman while 11 Indian seafarers were onboard.
Nine sailors have been rescued, while search operations continue for two missing Indians.
Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal on Sunday said that the tanker Mt Petro Dolphin, carrying 11 Indian seafarers, was subjected to a drone attack at Sohar Anchorage.
In a post on X, Sonowal said that while nine Indian crew members had been successfully rescued and were safe, two Indian nationals remained missing.
He further said search-and-rescue operations were actively underway by the local Coast Guard.

"We are continuously coordinating with all relevant authorities to fully support the ongoing rescue efforts and ensure every possible action is taken to safely locate our missing personnel," Sonowal said.

stories.headline: HC quashes PSA detention over two-year delay in execution
stories.title: HC quashes PSA detention over two-year delay in execution
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 11: The High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh has quashed a preventive detention order issued against Kaiser Hameed Beigh under the Public Safety Act (PSA), holding that the order was based on vague and irrelevant grounds and that an unexplained delay of more than two years in its execution had snapped the required “live and proximate link” between past alleged activities and the need for detention. Justice Rajesh Sekhri passed the judgment while allowing a petition challenging the detention order dated June 25, 2022, issued by the District Magistrate, Anantnag. The High Court had stayed the order on September 11, 2024, before its execution. According to the detention dossier, the Senior Superintendent of Police, Anantnag, had alleged that Beigh was an overground worker of the banned Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) outfit and had allegedly provided shelter and transportation to active terroristss. The authorities also cited his previous detention under the PSA in 2021 and apprehensions ahead of the Shri Amarnath Yatra as reasons for seeking fresh preventive detention. However, the petitioner argued that the allegations were vague, no fresh activities had been attributed to him after the earlier incidents, and the detention order was passed despite the absence of any immediate threat justifying his detention. He also challenged the delay in executing the order, pointing out that he had remained available and continued attending court proceedings. The authorities opposed the petition, maintaining that the detention order had been passed after considering the police dossier and that the petitioner’s alleged activities posed a threat to the security of the State. After examining the record, Justice Sekhri observed that the detention order appeared to have been passed on the apprehension that the petitioner’s alleged links with the banned outfit made it risky to keep him at liberty during the Amarnath Yatra. The court noted that the petitioner was regularly attending proceedings before the Additional Sessions Judge, Anantnag, in the single FIR of 2019 cited against him. Relying on the Supreme Court’s judgment in Additional Secretary to Government of India v. Alka Subash Gadia, the High Court held that pre-execution challenges to detention orders can be entertained in limited circumstances, including where orders are based on vague or irrelevant grounds or are issued for an improper purpose. The court further observed that preventive detention must be supported by a strong and immediate connection between past conduct and the present necessity for detention. The unexplained delay of over two years, it held, had severed that connection. “Viewed from any angle, the impugned order does not sustain in the eyes of law,” the court observed, quashing the detention order and allowing the petition.
